title: Trilateral Commission regional legal and secretariat structure pass, 2026-08-08
summary: Audit separating regional groups, legal entities, secretariat operators, contact addresses, and registered establishments across Europe and Asia Pacific, with Canada/Mexico legal status left unresolved.

sources.title: European Section of the Trilateral Commission - W751064404

evidence.observation: France's official business directory lists ASSOCIATION SECTION EUROPEENNE COMMISSION TRILATERALE, SIREN 507983153, as an active declared association and records active establishment SIRET 50798315300028 at 3 rue de Monttessuy, Paris, since 2023-11-24.

An RNA-derived index resolves W751064404 for the European section and reports creation on 1983-05-06 and latest declaration on 2024-12-20. The 1983 association history and 2008 SIRENE registration are preserved as separate registry events.

The Commission website publishes the European Group at 95 rue d’Amsterdam, while the French government directory records a different active establishment at 3 rue de Monttessuy. Contact/secretariat address and registered establishment must remain distinct fields.

JCIE states it served as Asia Pacific Secretariat from 1973 through 2024 and that International House of Japan took over from January 2025; I-House independently confirms serving as Asia-Pacific Secretariat since 2025.
International House of Japan identifies itself as a nonprofit established in 1952, headquartered at 5-11-16 Roppongi, and authorized as a Public Interest Incorporated Foundation from 2012.
The Commission footer shows the current I-House Roppongi address for Asia Pacific but still links www.jcie.or.jp after the 2025 secretariat transfer, indicating mixed field freshness.

gaps: A direct official RNA/JOAFE record for W751064404 should replace the RNA-derived secondary index when retrievable.
The formal relationship between the European registered association and the website's European secretariat/contact address remains unresolved.
Separate Canadian and Mexican legal entities have not been established by authoritative registry evidence in this pass.
The financial relationship between I-House and the Asia-Pacific Group as secretariat remains unresolved.
caveats: A regional secretariat operator is not automatically legally identical to the regional group.
A website contact address is not automatically the registered establishment of a legal entity.
Different registry dates can describe different administrative events and should not be collapsed into one founding date.
Operational participation by Canadian or Mexican officials does not establish separate incorporation.

workflow.next_action: Model Europe legal identity and Asia-Pacific secretariat succession through repository-scripted normalized writes; continue authoritative registry searches for Canada and Mexico.

notes: Europe has a source-backed French association identity, SIREN 507983153, distinct from the generic global Commission node.
JCIE operated the Asia-Pacific secretariat through 2024 and International House of Japan took over in January 2025.
The Commission footer mixes current I-House address data with a stale JCIE link, reinforcing the need for field-level freshness checks.
Canadian and Mexican legal-entity status remains unresolved and should not be guessed.

classification_rules: Separate regional group, legal entity, secretariat operator, contact address, and registered establishment.
Use SIREN/SIRET/RNA and equivalent jurisdictional identifiers for entity resolution.
Do not treat a stale regional website link as evidence of current operation when successor/operator sources disagree.
Keep Canada and Mexico legal identity unresolved until authoritative registry evidence exists.
data.method: Compared French business/association registry records with current Trilateral European contact data; cross-checked JCIE and International House of Japan statements on Asia-Pacific secretariat succession; tested Canada/Mexico for authoritative separate legal identities without promoting inconclusive search results.
data.narrative_role: regional legal-entity resolution, secretariat chronology, and stale-field audit
data.research_question: What legal and operational entities actually underlie the Commission's regional groups, and which relations must remain distinct from generic membership?

findings.finding: The European section has an active French declared-association identity, SIREN 507983153, with a currently active establishment distinct from the Commission website's secretariat address.
RNA-derived history places the European association's creation in 1983, while SIRENE registration begins in 2008; preserve both as different registry events.
JCIE served as Asia-Pacific Secretariat from 1973 through 2024 and International House of Japan took over from January 2025.
The current Commission footer combines I-House's current address with a stale JCIE domain link.
Authoritative separate Canadian and Mexican legal entities were not established in this pass and remain unresolved.
